title: Python Mini Projects
text:
Preface
Welcome to the Python Mini Projects collection! 👋
This book serves as a comprehensive guide and repository for a variety of easy-to-understand Python small projects. Whether you are a beginner looking to improve your programming skills or an expert seeking a playground to share knowledge, this collection has something for you.

title: Python Mini Projects
text:
Aim of the Project
As a Python newbie, I understand the problems that people face when they first begin studying and attempting to understand various Data Science concepts, particularly Python. This project is designed for folks who are just getting started with Python principles and exploring GitHub as “contributors.”
My goal is to build a common playground where everyone can learn and share knowledge.
Let’s “folk-ing” create amazing things together! 👉

title: 1  Introduction
text:
1.1 How to use this book
This book documents a collection of Python mini-projects. Each project is designed to be simple, educational, and easy to run.
You can browse the Projects list to find a project that interests you. Each project is located in its own directory in the GitHub repository.

title: 1  Introduction
text:
1.2 Contributing
We welcome contributions from everyone! If you have a simple Python project you’d like to share:

Fork the repository.
Clone your fork.
Create a folder for your project.
Add your code and a README.md.
Submit a Pull Request.

For more detailed instructions, please refer to the repository README.

title: 3  Summary
text:
In summary, this collection provides over 100 mini-projects to help you learn Python. From simple games like “Henman” and “Snake” to more advanced tools like “Address Validator” and “Face Recognition”, there is plenty to explore and learn from.
We hope you find these projects useful for your learning journey!
